You seem to misunderstand how colour works/how we see it. If you're looking at something that is, say, blue, it absorbs all the other wavelengths of light except for the one specific wavelength - that shade is reflected back into your eyes and is interpreted by your brain as being blue. When an object is black, it absorbs all the wavelengths of light and doesn't reflect any back...it isn't an absence of colour, it is an absence of the reflection of any specific wavelength of light, and your brain interprets it as black. The opposite is true for white. A white object - not white like our skin, white like a sheet of printer paper - reflects all wavelengths of light, and so our brain interprets it as being white because it is an unbroken spectrum of light.

Black people aren't really black and white people aren't really white. We aren't beams of light. However, we do generally have more contrasting colours in our complexion - black people usually have dark skin, dark eyes, dark hair, and darker lips, while we have more colour options for our eyes and hair and lips. We are more colourful, in short.
